---
title: "A first model"
---

Fit a linear model to ten flats, read the estimates, and predict rents for flats that are not in the data.

The page runs with the [extension](installation.qmd) or the plain-PHP [polyfill](extension-or-polyfill.qmd). The data are simulated: `rent` is the monthly rent in an unnamed currency, `area` is the floor area in square meters, and `district` is one of three districts.

## Data

The formula functions take named columns: an associative array of `column => list of values`, with every column the same length. A table object with `toModelData()` or `toColumns()`, such as a phibble `DataFrame`, is also accepted.

```php
use function Phit\{fit_ols, predict};

$flats = [
    'rent' => [
        1879.25, 1805.03, 2022.29, 1267.85, 1509.24,
        2240.10, 959.51, 2386.54, 1655.80, 1420.00,
    ],
    'area' => [
        74.4, 57.4, 66.4, 49.1, 45.7,
        92.4, 37.0, 93.9, 61.2, 52.3,
    ],
    'district' => [
        'north', 'south', 'north', 'east', 'south',
        'north', 'east', 'south', 'east', 'south',
    ],
];
```

- Numeric values make a numeric column.
- Strings make a factor whose levels sort in byte order, so `east` is the reference level.
- [Model formulas](formulas.qmd#data) lists every accepted column type.

## Fit

```php
$fit = fit_ols('rent ~ area + district', $flats);
```

`rent` is the response. `area + district` adds a slope for floor area and treatment-coded indicators for the districts. The intercept is included unless the formula removes it with `- 1` or `+ 0`.

## Read the result

The result is a PHP array. Every per-coefficient list follows the order of `columns`.

```php
foreach ($fit['columns'] as $i => $name) {
    printf(
        "%-14s %8.2f %7.2f %7.4f\n",
        $name,
        $fit['coefficients'][$i],
        $fit['std_errors'][$i],
        $fit['p_values'][$i],
    );
}
```

```
(Intercept)      352.64  179.87  0.0976
area              19.18    3.23  0.0010
districtnorth    203.64  151.14  0.2265
districtsouth    232.16  119.64  0.1004
```

- The `area` coefficient is the difference in rent associated with one more square meter, among flats in the same district.
- Each district coefficient is the difference from `east` for flats of the same area.

| Key | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `columns`, `named` | Coefficient names, and a `name => coefficient` map |
| `coefficients`, `std_errors`, `t_statistics`, `p_values` | One value per column |
| `conf_int` | 95% intervals, `[lower, upper]` per column |
| `covariance` | The coefficient covariance matrix |
| `fitted`, `residuals` | One value per retained row |
| `r_squared`, `adj_r_squared`, `sigma`, `rss`, `log_likelihood`, `df_residual` | Fit statistics |
| `n_input`, `n_observations`, `n_dropped`, `retained_rows`, `dropped_rows` | Sample accounting |
| `diagnostics` | Solver, convergence, and warnings |

```php
printf(
    "R-squared %.4f, sigma %.2f, %d residual df\n",
    $fit['r_squared'],
    $fit['sigma'],
    $fit['df_residual'],
);
echo json_encode($fit['diagnostics']), "\n";
```

```
R-squared 0.9270, sigma 146.29, 6 residual df
{"converged":true,"solver":"scaled_svd","warnings":[]}
```

`fit_generalized_linear()`, `fit_mixed_gaussian()`, and `fit_mixed_logistic()` return the same naming and accounting keys with the statistics of their model. See [Linear and generalized linear models](models.qmd) and [Mixed models](mixed-models.qmd).

## Predict

`predict()` rebuilds the formula over new data. The response column is not needed, and factor levels are those the fit saw.

```php
$new = [
    'area' => [55.0, 80.0],
    'district' => ['east', 'north'],
];
$p = predict($fit, $new, interval: 'prediction');

foreach ($p['fit'] as $i => $value) {
    printf(
        "%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]\n",
        $value,
        $p['lower'][$i],
        $p['upper'][$i],
    );
}
```

```
1407.55 [991.59, 1823.51]
2090.69 [1676.97, 2504.41]
```

- `interval: 'prediction'` covers one new flat's rent. `interval: 'confidence'` covers the mean rent.
- A district the fit never saw throws an exception with code 1001.
- [Prediction](formulas.qmd#prediction-predict) covers generalized linear and mixed-model predictions.

## Missing values

`null` and `NAN` are missing. By default, a row with a missing value in any column the formula uses is dropped, and the fit emits one `E_WARNING`. With `rent` set to `null` in the third row, the warning reads:

```
Phit\fit_ols(): Phit\fit_ols dropped 1 of 10 observations with missing values (listwise deletion)
```

- The result reports `n_observations` 9, `n_input` 10, and `dropped_rows` `[2]`.
- `diagnostics.warnings` records `listwise deletion removed 1 of 10 original rows`.
- `missing: 'raise'` rejects missing values. The call throws an `Exception` with code 1001 and the message `missing values found with missing='raise'`.

[Missing values](missing-data.qmd) defines which values count as missing and how rows are counted.

## Errors

Invalid input and failed fits throw a PHP `Exception`. `getCode()` gives the category, for example:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 1001 | Invalid input |
| 1002 | Mismatched lengths |
| 1004 | Rank-deficient design |
| 1006 | Nonconvergence |

The full table is in the [API overview](contracts.qmd#v01-diagnostics-and-errors).
